F.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Kirby (Nintendo / HAL Laboratory) — the official character café

F.n: Isetan Shinjuku Depachika (伊勢丹新宿店 食品フロア)
F.ad: Isetan Shinjuku main store B1, 3-14-1 Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
F.w: The flagship Isetan's basement food hall — one of Tokyo's poshest depachika, renovated in 2023, with a fresh market of tasting counters (ham, sausage, oden) and Café Prunier Paris for caviar and champagne.

F.n: Ginza Mitsukoshi Depachika (銀座三越 食品フロア)
F.ad: Ginza Mitsukoshi B2–B3, Ginza 4-chōme, Chūō-ku, Tokyo
F.w: Two basement floors under Ginza's landmark department store: B2 for prepared food, Japanese and Western sweets and bakeries; B3 a gourmet supermarket with an outstanding cheese counter and perfect Japanese fruit.

F.n: Asakusa Oden Otafuku (浅草おでん 大多福)
F.w: Founded in 1915 and one of Tokyo's oldest oden houses — paper lanterns, a kept garden and pots of oden simmering in light dashi; a former Michelin Bib Gourmand.

F.n: Unagi Komagata Maekawa (駒形 前川)
F.ad: Komagata, Taitō-ku, Tokyo (on the Sumida River near Asakusa Station)
F.w: An Edo-period eel wholesaler turned restaurant on the Sumida riverbank: unagi grilled and steamed until fluffy, lacquered with a tare the house says has not changed in 220 years.

F.n: Daikokuya Tempura, Asakusa (大黒家天麩羅)
F.ad: Near Sensō-ji (Denbōin-dōri side), Asakusa, Taitō-ku, Tokyo
F.w: A stone's throw from Sensō-ji, the best known of Asakusa's old tempura houses (alongside San Sada and Owariya), with queues for its tempura and tendon.

The Fukuoka tonkotsu chain famous for customising noodle firmness, richness, garlic and spring onion on a paper form and slurping alone in a partitioned booth — a rite of passage for first-time visitors.
Blue Bottle's first café outside the US (2015), set in a converted warehouse — its arrival made Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Tokyo's specialty-coffee neighbourhood.
A 1930 sweets parlour that escaped wartime damage and still trades from its original wooden building, a designated historic structure — famous for agemanjū and old-school wagashi.

F.ad: Residential street ~10 min walk from Shimokitazawa Station, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
F.w: A traditional house with a small garden on a quiet Shimokitazawa backstreet, drawing soba connoisseurs from across the city for hand-cut noodles — try the yuba soba or mitsuba soba.
Jimbōchō kissaten opened in 1949 in a narrow alley of the book town, a long-standing literary hangout; credited with introducing Vienna coffee to Japan.
Iconic Jimbōchō kissaten in business since 1955, known for its cottage-style front and tiki-like interior crammed with trinkets gifted by regulars.
Kissaten in a 1916 Yanaka building, run as a coffee shop from 1938 to 2006 and reopened in 2009 with the original exterior and signage; known for its egg sandwich.

F.n: Arise Coffee Roasters (アライズコーヒーロースターズ)
F.w: Small single-origin roaster in an old corner shop in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Tokyo's coffee district; the owner hand-pours each cup and chats with regulars.
Tiny Nishi-Shinjuku whisky bar with about 300 bottles, over a hundred of them Japanese incl. sold-out limited editions; the cinephile owner screens silent films while you drink.

F.n: Goodbeer Faucets Shibuya (グッドビアフォウセッツ 渋谷)
F.w: Shibuya craft-beer bar open since 2012 with one of the city's largest tap lists (40+ Japanese, US and European beers) and a well-known happy hour.

F.n: Baird Beer Nakameguro Taproom (ベアードタップルーム中目黒)
F.ad: 2F Nakameguro Gate Town, 2-1-3 Kamimeguro, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
F.w: First Tokyo pub of Numazu's Baird Brewing, a brick-and-wood taproom pouring Baird's own beers alongside New Haven-style pizza.

F.n: Azuki to Kouri (あずきとこおり)
F.w: Seven-seat, reservation-only kakigōri counter in Yoyogi-Uehara opened in January 2022 by pastry chef Miho Horio (ex-Florilège); signature azuki-and-meringue shaved ice.
Residential-Nakano shaved-ice shop of Asako Harada, the 'Kakigōri Queen' said to have eaten some 1,800 bowls in a year; known for mountainous, painterly bowls such as seasonal fruit with sake lees.
Eight-seat counter izakaya a short walk from central Shibuya; the sake sommelier is a hot-sake specialist warming each pour to a precise temperature, paired with a good-value omakase.

F.n: Meikyoku Kissa Lion (名曲喫茶ライオン)
F.w: Tokyo's oldest and best-known classical-music café, first opened in 1926 and rebuilt in 1950; pew-like seats face a 3m Pioneer speaker wall and conversation is discouraged.
Yotsuya kissaten started in 1954 by the father of current owner Hiroaki Ogura, profiled by Monocle among Tokyo's enduring independent kissaten; a regular haunt of visiting jazz band The Lagerphones.
Small Dogenzaka record bar whose name stands for Jazz, Blues and Soul; over 11,000 LPs line the walls and the owner spins from them.
Wagashi shop by Gokokuji Station renowned for its large mame-daifuku, mochi wrapped around anko with slightly salty whole beans kneaded in, still sold cheaply.
Kuramae specialty coffee flagship offering tasting courses and around 20 filtered coffees, many rare single origins bought at auction, with an omakase-style coffee experience.

F.n: Dandelion Chocolate Factory & Café Kuramae (ダンデライオン・チョコレート 蔵前)
F.w: Tokyo home of the San Francisco bean-to-bar chocolatier: half café, half factory, where you watch chocolate made through the glass and order the brownie flight.

F.n: Obscura Coffee Roasters — Café Obscura, Sangenjaya (オブスキュラ コーヒーロースターズ)
F.w: Sangenjaya roaster founded in 2009 and credited with seeding the district's specialty coffee scene; its gallery-like main café specialises in siphon coffee with two house blends and rotating single origins.
The shop that started iekei ramen in 1974 — the 家 in 'iekei' honours Yoshimura-ya; its tonkotsu-shoyu soup with spinach and nori spawned Yokohama's whole iekei style.
Kawagoe eel house founded in 1807 whose secret kabayaki sauce has been passed down to the seventh generation; cited as serving one of Japan's most renowned grilled unagi.

F.ad: 2458 Higashi-Koiji, Funatsu, Fujikawaguchiko, Minamitsuru District, Yamanashi 〒401-0301
F.w: Fuji Five Lakes hōtō specialist that makes its flat noodles in house; each diner gets a giant pot of hōtō in miso broth with kabocha and cabbage, and queues are common. A second branch is at 2746-1 Kawaguchi, Fujikawaguchiko.

F.n: Udatsu Sushi, Nakameguro (宇田津 鮨)
F.w: Hisashi Udatsu's art-gallery-like sushi counter hidden in Nakameguro's backstreets — textbook nigiri that sneaks in surprises, with paintings on the walls; listed in the MICHELIN Guide.

F.ad: On the Meguro River, Aobadai, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
F.w: Opened March 2019 as the fifth and then-largest Starbucks Reserve Roastery: a four-floor Kengo Kuma building clad in Japanese cedar beside the Meguro River's cherry trees, roasting on site with coffee cocktails upstairs.

F.ad: Near JR Kamata Station, Kamata, Ōta-ku, Tokyo
F.w: Where Dalian-born Isao Yagi invented hanetsuki ('winged') gyōza, pouring flour-water into the pan for a crisp lattice — the reason Kamata calls itself the birthplace of winged dumplings.

Frying tonkatsu since 1939 with hardly a change: a long counter wraps the open kitchen so diners watch the cooks at work, and the benches round the room are always full of people queuing for a counter seat.

F.n: Tofuya Ukai, Shiba-kōen (とうふ屋うかい)
F.w: A samurai-era merchant's residence and carp-pond garden at the foot of Tokyo Tower (its 'borrowed scenery'), serving tofu kaiseki built on Hokkaido-bean tofu made each morning in the Okutama mountains.

F.ad: 1F, Garden City Shinagawa Gotenyama, 6-7-29 Kitashinagawa, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo 141-0001
F.w: Chef Shuzo Kishida's modern French dining room in Gotenyama — one of Tokyo's eleven three-MICHELIN-star restaurants in the 2026 guide.

F.n: RyuGin, Tokyo Midtown Hibiya (日本料理 龍吟)
F.ad: 7F, Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, 1-1-2 Yūrakuchō, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-0006
F.w: Seiji Yamamoto's celebrated Japanese restaurant, moved from Roppongi to the 7th floor of Tokyo Midtown Hibiya — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

F.n: Kioicho Fukudaya (紀尾井町 福田家)
F.w: A traditional ryōtei in Kioichō serving seasonal Japanese cuisine — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
Takahashi Harutaka's Ginza Edomae sushi counter — three MICHELIN stars ('exceptional cuisine') in the 2026 guide.

F.n: Azabu Kadowaki (麻布 かどわき)
F.w: Toshiya Kadowaki's Azabu-Jūban Japanese restaurant — three MICHELIN stars ('exceptional cuisine') in the 2026 guide.
Tomoya Kawada's Minami-Azabu Chinese restaurant in a quiet house — one of Tokyo's eleven three-MICHELIN-star restaurants in the 2026 guide.
Shiseido's historic Ginza French restaurant, opened in 1973 — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

F.n: L'Effervescence, Nishi-Azabu (レフェルヴェソンス)
F.w: Shinobu Namae's Nishi-Azabu restaurant fusing French technique and Japanese produce — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

F.n: Joël Robuchon, Yebisu Garden Place (ジョエル・ロブション)
F.ad: Yebisu Garden Place, 1-13-1 Mita, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
F.w: The late Joël Robuchon's flagship Tokyo dining room in the faux-château at Yebisu Garden Place (Meguro-ku side) — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

F.n: Sushi Kanesaka, Ginza (鮨 かねさか)
F.w: Shinji Kanesaka's basement Ginza sushi counter, the mothership of a group with branches abroad — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.
A small Jingūmae restaurant holding two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
Nakameguro restaurant promoted from one to two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

Chef Yamamoto's basement Japanese restaurant in Mita — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide; inspectors note that for all his innovations he stays true to tradition with wansashi, sashimi paired with soup.
Fine-dining restaurant in the Kabutochō financial quarter — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

F.ad: 3F, Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioichō, 1-3 Kioichō, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 102-0094
F.w: Tasting-menu restaurant on the third floor of Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioichō — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.
Shintomi restaurant listed with two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
One-MICHELIN-star Kagurazaka Japanese restaurant whose forte is charcoal grilling, each ingredient handled with the strictest attention.
'In simple honesty' — a phrase handed down from the chef's two mentors names this one-MICHELIN-star Kagurazaka Japanese restaurant and its plain-spoken cooking.
One-MICHELIN-star Kagurazaka restaurant aiming for the unexpected through a trinity of food, sake and serving vessels.
Shinjuku 1-chōme sushi counter newly awarded one MICHELIN star in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
Asakusa restaurant holding one MICHELIN star ('high quality cooking') in the 2026 guide — the district's starred table beyond the tempura and unagi houses.
A Bib Gourmand trattoria near Tomioka Hachimangū where the chef's love of Tuscany shows in chicken-liver crostini, Florentine tripe and hand-rolled pici.
A Japanese restaurant in shitamachi Morishita, selected by the MICHELIN Guide (2026 selection).
A Chinese restaurant in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa's Miyoshi district, selected by the MICHELIN Guide (2026 selection).
A contemporary restaurant in Sumida's Yokokawa district, selected by the MICHELIN Guide (2026 selection).
A Bib Gourmand in residential Setagaya whose creative cooking is designed around its affinity with sake — meat dishes are an indispensable part of the menu.
A French Bib Gourmand in Ikejiri, near Ikejiri-Ōhashi — good-value cooking in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide.
A French Bib Gourmand in the Kitazawa (Shimokitazawa) backstreets — good quality, good value cooking in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide.

F.ad: Shibamata 7-chōme, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo (from Shibamata Station to Taishakuten)
F.w: The 200-metre Edo-era approach to Shibamata Taishakuten, lined with wooden shops selling the town's speciality kusa-dango and restaurants serving river fish such as eel and carp — the setting of the Tora-san films.

F.ad: 1-18-8 Tateishi, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo (inside Tateishi Nakamise arcade)
F.w: Tateishi's legendary motsuyaki counter in the post-war Nakamise arcade — a queue of 30 forms before the 2pm opening for grilled innards, stew and pickles at ¥200 a plate, with an ordering shorthand regulars help newcomers through.

F.ad: By Kita-Senju Station West Exit, Senju, Adachi-ku, Tokyo
F.w: A drinking alley off Kita-Senju's west exit that keeps the old yokochō charm — salarymen and Tokyo Denki University students pack its izakaya, where Kabura-ya grills skewers for under ¥100.

F.ad: Nomiya Yokochō area by Kita-Senju Station West Exit, Adachi-ku, Tokyo
F.w: A bottle-shop-cum-standing-bar in Kita-Senju's drinking alley with around 1,500 bottled beers to drink on the spot.
A Kichijōji butcher whose ground-floor counter draws queues for its maru menchi croquettes, with a wagyu steak restaurant on the floor above.

F.ad: 4-13-15 Kichijōji, Musashino, Tokyo (end of Nakamichi shopping street)
F.w: A blue-fronted micro-roastery opened in 2014 at the end of Kichijōji's Nakamichi street by two young roasters — single origins in signature blue cups, cuppings and roasting workshops.
Kichijōji's Alice-in-Wonderland-inspired café where shaved ice is cloaked in meringue and set on fire, the flaming sauce changing with the flavour.

F.n: Sugoi Niboshi Ramen Nagi, Golden Gai (すごい煮干ラーメン凪)
F.ad: 2F, Shinjuku Golden Gai (G2 Street), 1-1-10 Kabukichō, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
F.w: Up a steep stair in an old wooden Golden Gai house, the Nagi chain's 2008 return to its birthplace serves pungent niboshi ramen from sardines boiled for 12 hours — open 24 hours.

F.n: Togoshi Ginza Shōtengai (戸越銀座商店街)
F.ad: Togoshi, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo (around Togoshi-ginza Station, Tōkyū Ikegami line)
F.w: Tokyo's longest open-air shopping street — 1.3 km and some 400 shops — where more than 20 shops fry croquettes for snacking on the walk, between yakitori, yakisoba and dango stands.
A French bistro near Jiyūgaoka from a chef schooled in both Tokyo and Paris kitchens — Bib Gourmand in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide.

F.n: Mont St. Clair, Jiyūgaoka (モンサンクレール)
F.w: A patisserie in Jiyūgaoka, Tokyo's 'Little Europe' of sweet shops — its tall cone-shaped Mont Blanc and Rihei-chestnut version make Time Out's best Mont Blancs in Tokyo.

F.ad: A few minutes' walk from Sangenjaya Station, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
F.w: Sangenjaya's 'triangle' — a maze of alleys a few minutes from the station packed with old-school and new-wave pubs, yakitori joints and curry counters, a very local yokochō that redevelopment has passed by.
A six-seat counter in the Sankaku Chitai triangle pouring spirits infused with medicinal herbs and oddities from goji berries and lavender to broiled eel.

F.ad: By Tomioka Hachimangū, Monzen-Nakachō, Kōtō-ku, Tokyo
F.w: The go-to for Fukagawa-meshi, the late-Edo fishermen's clam rice of this old fishing district — the poured-over version is made fresh to order with richly sweet miso and freshly harvested clams.

F.n: Chanko Tomoegata, Ryōgoku (ちゃんこ巴潟)
F.w: Sumo town's favourite chanko-nabe house for nearly 50 years — the wrestlers' hot pot served as lunch sets that change by weekday (pork miso on Tuesdays, duck dumplings on Wednesdays) and by season.

One of Ueno's most popular ramen counters: only Japanese duck and leek, simmered for two days into a clear, sweet, ungamey stock with house-made noodles — the anchor of the Okachimachi 'ramen yokochō' cluster.

F.n: Yanaka Ginza Shōtengai (谷中銀座商店街)
F.ad: Yanaka 3-chōme, Taitō-ku, Tokyo (between Nippori and Sendagi stations, below the Yūyake Dandan steps)
F.w: A 60-shop old-Tokyo shopping street between Nippori and Sendagi, best grazed: beef menchi katsu from Niku no Suzuki (since 1980), cat-shaped taiyaki, manjū and matcha, all below the 'sunset steps'.
Kokubunji's ramen standout, run by alumni of Nagi and Gamushara: the signature 'wahaha' niboshi chūka soba alongside a chicken 'gahaha' and an 'ahaha' tsukemen.

F.n: Tsukemen Enji, Kichijōji (つけ麺 えん寺)
F.w: A hugely popular Kichijōji tsukemen shop and a food-magazine favourite, known for the bamboo mat in the noodle bowl that drains stray broth.

F.n: Ozawa Shuzo — Sawanoi Sake Brewery, Ōme (小澤酒造 澤乃井)
F.ad: Sawai, Ōme, Tokyo (a few steps from JR Sawai Station, on the Tama River)
F.w: Tokyo's oldest brewery, founded 1702 in the Okutama hills: free tours of kura buildings over 300 years old, then a tunnel to the riverside Sawanoi-en garden to taste ten sakes by the cup — plus a sake shop and tofu restaurants.

F.ad: Fussa, Tokyo (near the Tama River, ~20 min walk from JR Haijima Station)
F.w: A sake brewery since 1863 (Tamajiman) that revived beer-making in 1998 after a 111-year pause — tour 19th-century kura and the Zougura museum, then drink Tama no Megumi or Tokyo Blues at the on-site Italian beer hall.

Founded in the last years of the 19th century and rebuilt after the 1923 earthquake in the two-storey timber house it still occupies: one dish only, chicken sukiyaki bubbling in a cast-iron pot over glowing charcoal.

F.n: Curry Bondy, Jimbōchō (欧風カレー ボンディ)
F.w: The Jimbōchō shop credited with creating 'European-style' curry — a roux built on veal stock and demi-glace simmered over days; up a flight above a bookshop, queues at lunch, and first winner of the Kanda Curry Grand Prix (2011).
